artifact.summary: Gate-level Qiskit implementation of the Toffoli (CCNOT) target unitary from eq_1, with configurable control and target qubits on a register of 3 to 12 qubits. An optional flag selects the standard H/T/Tdg/CX decomposition instead of the native ccx gate. The paper's pulse-level control, Hamiltonian, and Differential Evolution optimization are not implemented.
artifact.source_python:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, QuantumRegister


def _as_int(value, name):
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
        raise ValueError(name + ' must be an integer')
    return value


def build_circuit(instance):
    """Toffoli: |a,b,c> -> |a,b,c xor (a and b)> (eq_1).

    instance keys: num_qubits (3..12, default 3), controls (two distinct indices,
    default [0, 1]), target (index, default 2), decompose (bool, default False).
    """
    if not isinstance(instance, dict):
        raise ValueError('instance must be a dict')
    n = _as_int(instance.get('num_qubits', 3), 'num_qubits')
    if n < 3 or n > 12:
        raise ValueError('num_qubits must be in [3, 12]')
    controls = instance.get('controls', [0, 1])
    if not isinstance(controls, (list, tuple)) or len(controls) != 2:
        raise ValueError('controls must contain exactly two indices')
    a = _as_int(controls[0], 'control')
    b = _as_int(controls[1], 'control')
    t = _as_int(instance.get('target', 2), 'target')
    for q in (a, b, t):
        if q < 0 or q >= n:
            raise ValueError('qubit index out of range')
    if len({a, b, t}) != 3:
        raise ValueError('controls and target must be distinct')
    decompose = instance.get('decompose', False)
    if not isinstance(decompose, bool):
        raise ValueError('decompose must be a bool')
    qr = QuantumRegister(n, 'q')
    qc = QuantumCircuit(qr)
    if not decompose:
        qc.ccx(a, b, t)
    else:
        qc.h(t)
        qc.cx(b, t)
        qc.tdg(t)
        qc.cx(a, t)
        qc.t(t)
        qc.cx(b, t)
        qc.tdg(t)
        qc.cx(a, t)
        qc.t(b)
        qc.t(t)
        qc.h(t)
        qc.cx(a, b)
        qc.t(a)
        qc.tdg(b)
        qc.cx(a, b)
    return qc
register_layout: q2: target c (flipped iff q0 and q1 are both 1)
Optional q3..q11: idle spectator qubits if num_qubits > 3
Computational basis: Qiskit little-endian, qubit 0 is the least significant bit

equation_mapping.code_location: build_circuit (qc.ccx, or the H/T/Tdg/CX decomposition when decompose is true)
equation_mapping.explanation: The Toffoli action |a,b,c> -> |a,b,c xor (a and b)> is applied as a gate on the chosen control and target qubits.
The time-ordered propagator describes how a pulse-level gate would be generated. It is context only, and no time evolution is simulated.
The transmon-chain Hamiltonian is an unconfirmed placeholder. Its parameters and controls are unspecified and pulse-level physics is outside this gate-level circuit.
The fidelity is an evaluation metric that needs operator construction, which the generated module must not do. Software outside the module can evaluate it.
The Differential Evolution optimization is a classical loop over pulse parameters. Its enhanced and non-greedy details are unavailable and it is not a quantum circuit operation.

specification_changes.change: Narrowed scope to the gate-level Toffoli target unitary (eq_1) only. No pulse-level control, Hamiltonian evolution, fidelity computation, or Differential Evolution optimization is implemented.
specification_changes.reason: The Hamiltonian parameters, pulse parametrization, gate time, and optimizer details are missing. Operator construction and optimization are not allowed in the generated module.

specification_changes.change: Generalized the qubit labels (a,b,c) to configurable distinct indices on a register of 3 to 12 qubits, with defaults q0 and q1 as controls and q2 as target. This follows Qiskit little-endian ordering instead of a written (a,b,c) ordering.
specification_changes.reason: Gives the operation varying valid parameters while preserving the Toffoli action.

assumptions: The default qubit order maps a to q0, b to q1, and c to q2.
The standard H/T/Tdg/CX decomposition is an exact Toffoli up to no extra global phase, so it equals ccx.
The circuit is closed-system, measurement-free, and unitary.
unresolved_issues: The paper's pulse-level single-shot implementation cannot be reconstructed from the abstract.
No gate duration or transmon parameters are available.
The fidelity definition and leakage handling remain assumptions.
